# Parley v0.1.35

A robustness release. Nothing new to use; several ways Parley could get stuck,
lose its coordination history, or report a delivery that had not happened are
closed.

The findings came from a cross-vendor review — Agy read the native code, and
each finding was checked against the source before anything was changed. Three
of its seven described a worse outcome than the code actually produced, and
those corrections are noted below rather than quietly dropped.

## Handoff history survives a failed write

This is the one worth restarting for.

Parley's handoff journal appends one synced line per record. If that append
failed part-way — a full disk, a process killed mid-write — the partial bytes
stayed on disk. The next append then began in the middle of that unfinished
line and fused the two into a record nothing could decode. On the next launch
the coordination core refused to start: panes still ran, but relay, Ask,
Delegate and history were unavailable until the file was repaired or deleted by
hand, and that state survived every restart.

The journal now records where the last acknowledged record ended and cuts back
to that boundary when an append fails. If it cannot cut them away, it rewrites
the file from the records it has already acknowledged before appending anything
after them. The activity journal has worked this way for some time; the handoff
journal now matches it.

One deliberate behaviour is kept: a relay that has already reached a live
terminal stays in Parley's view of the conversation even if writing it down
fails, because the message really was delivered. That exception was always
about memory, never about leaving damaged bytes on disk.

## A pane that could not attach now recovers

If a pane's terminal surface was briefly unavailable while Parley was attaching
it — during a workspace restore, before the pane list had been published — the
pane showed a short error message instead. It then kept showing it. There was
no path back for the life of that view, and a pane that recovered without being
restarted never got one, so the only way out was switching workspaces and back.

Parley now attaches the surface when it becomes available.

## A delivery into a closing pane refuses instead of reporting success

Sending text to a pane takes several steps, and between them Parley lets the
terminal catch up. A pane can be closed, stopped or restarted during those
pauses. Parley continued the delivery into the surface it started with, which
by then could already have been torn down — so a submission could be recorded
that never reached anything.

Each step that sends input now confirms the pane is still the one the delivery
started against, and refuses if it is not. Restoring your focus afterwards
deliberately does not: by then the text has landed, and failing there would
report a submission that actually happened and invite you to send it twice.

## A timed-out command can no longer hold a thread

When a command passes its deadline, Parley signals it and waits. The final wait
after `SIGKILL` had no bound. A process stuck in an uninterruptible system wait
— a hung network mount, an unresponsive filesystem — cannot be killed until
that wait finishes, so Parley would wait with it, indefinitely, defeating the
timeout it had just enforced. That wait is now bounded like the others and
reports the timeout either way.

## A backward clock step no longer freezes the window

The pauses between delivery steps were measured against the wall clock. If the
system clock stepped backward during one — an NTP correction — the pause held
for the length of the step with the main thread spinning, freezing the window
until the clock caught up. They are measured against a clock that only moves
forward.

## Internal work

Reading handoff history no longer locks the workspace model when there is no
delegation in flight, which is the usual state. This was reported as a cost paid
every second; it is not, because the refresh already skips its work when nothing
has changed. The wasted lock was real, the frequency was not, and both are in
the record.

## The open question from v0.1.34, answered

The v0.1.34 notes said a permission profile's execution rule had been confirmed
present in a pane's launch arguments and confirmed to block a command in a
non-interactive session, but that nobody had observed whether an interactive
session actually shows a prompt.

It does. Driving a real interactive session with the exact settings Parley
generates — hooks and all — and changing only whether the permission rule was
present: without it the command ran with no prompt, with it the session asked
for permission and left the command unrun. That is the behaviour the v0.1.34
notes could not claim.

## Compatibility

Agent protocol is unchanged at 32. The journal repair applies from this build
onward; a file already damaged by an earlier version is not rewritten
automatically, so if coordination is reporting itself unavailable, that file
still needs removing once.

Validated: 335 native checks, 53 Node tests, public scan, platform scan, build
and the 25-round eight-pane Ghostty soak with 200 delivered inputs. The journal
and timeout fixes were each watched failing before they were made. The pane
recovery and the clock change have no automated check — the first is in a target
the check suite cannot reach, the second is a property of the code rather than
of a behaviour — and neither is claimed as tested.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
